mainTopic: רבי חייא's two rulings on oaths: the הצד השוה source for witnesses on part of a loan, and the debate with רב ששת over whether one who says הילך must swear.
overview: This amud picks up in the middle of the גמרא's search for a source for רבי חייא's rule: if two witnesses prove a borrower owes part of a loan, he must swear about the rest. After a comparison to a single witness (עד אחד) fails, רב פפא suggests learning from גלגול שבועה. The גמרא then goes back and forth between a person's own admission (פיו) and עד אחד, with each one covering the other's weakness. In the end it combines them into a הצד השוה: both come through a claim and a denial, and so do witnesses. Two challenges to this, that he is a proven denier and that witnesses are subject to הזמה, are both answered. Next the גמרא says our משנה of two people holding a garment does not really match the witnesses case. Instead it supports a different ruling of רבי חייא: one who admits part of a claim and hands it over (הילך) must still swear. רב ששת disagrees and holds that הילך is exempt, calling the משנה's oath only rabbinic. רבי חייא answers that the חכמים model their oaths on Torah oaths. The amud ends as the גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא against רבי חייא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the rejection: witnesses are different from one witness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its rejection of the proof from עד אחד. With one witness the oath is about what the witness said, but with two witnesses the defendant would be swearing about the part he denied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say the same about two witnesses? In that case he swears about what he denied, not about what the witnesses testified to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a rejection that started just before this section. It explains why the case of one witness cannot prove the case of two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עד אחד, the defendant swears to deny exactly what the witness said. With two עדים, the witnesses settle the part they testified about, and any oath would be about a different part, the part he denied. Because these are different kinds of oaths, the comparison fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses; here, two kosher witnesses whose testimony is full proof
He denied (the claim)
He swears / takes an oath
'Would you say?', the second half of a 'מה ל...' rejection

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an argument that began before this section. It is not a new statement, so read it as the second half of 'what is special about one witness...'.

phrases.english: Would you say the same about witnesses,
where he swears about what he denied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection of 'עד אחד יוכיח' from before this section.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using עד אחד as a source for רבי חייא's קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With עד אחד the oath is about the same thing the witness testified to. With עדים the oath would be about a different part, the part that was denied.

steps.title: רב פפא: the source is the rolling-over oath from one witness
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא offers a new source: גלגול שבועה in the case of עד אחד. Once one witness makes a person swear, other claims can be added onto that oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: the proof comes from the 'rolling over' of an oath caused by one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier comparison failed, רב פפא suggests a different source for רבי חייא's קל וחומר. He points to גלגול שבועה, the rule that an oath can carry extra claims along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With גלגול, the oath for the extra claims was never caused by a witness to those claims; it was carried along by another oath. רב פפא argues: if that weak cause can lead to an oath on unproven claims, two witnesses on part of a claim should surely lead to an oath on the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals dropping the previous approach for a new one
'Rolling over' an oath: once someone must swear, other claims can be added to the same oath
One witness, whose testimony obligates the defendant to swear
It comes (is derived) from

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
It is derived from the rolling-over of an oath caused by one witness.
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי חייא's קל וחומר about witnesses on part of a claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected עד אחד proof with a different proof based on עד אחד's גלגול.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for the same law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר seemed to have no solid base after the עד אחד comparison failed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Base the קל וחומר on גלגול שבועה דעד אחד.

steps.title: Rejection: an oath pulling an oath is different from witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's source. With גלגול, one oath leads to another oath, but witnesses create a money obligation, which may not lead to an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about the rolling-over oath of one witness? There, one oath pulls along another oath. Would you say the same about witnesses, who make him owe money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's source by showing a difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In גלגול, the thing causing the new oath is itself an oath, so it is natural for an oath to bring another oath. Witnesses do not create an oath; they create a money debt. A money debt might not bring an oath along with it, so the קל וחומר fails.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath drags along another oath
Money; a monetary obligation
They obligate / make him liable
'What is special about X, since...', the formula for rejecting a קל וחומר

phrases.english: What is special about the rolling-over of an oath from one witness?
That there, an oath drags along an oath.
Would you say the same about witnesses,
who make him liable for money?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְגִלְגּוּל שְׁבוּעָה דְּעֵד אֶחָד, שֶׁכֵּן שְׁבוּעָה גּוֹרֶרֶת שְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's proposed source.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from גלגול שבועה דעד אחד.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In גלגול the cause is an oath, which can pull another oath. Witnesses only create a money obligation.

steps.title: Defense: a person's own admission proves it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that admission (פיו, the מודה במקצת case) shows that a money obligation can also lead to an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: His own mouth will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by pointing to a case where something other than an oath leads to an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person admits part of a claim, his admission makes him owe money, not swear, and yet he must swear about the rest. So the idea that 'only an oath can pull an oath' is shown to be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: His mouth; his own admission of part of the claim
Will prove; used to bring a counter-example
One who admits part of the claim and must swear about the rest

phrases.english: His mouth will prove it.
phrases.notes: His admission makes him owe money, not swear, yet it still obligates him to swear about the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 3 with a counter-example.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only an oath can bring another oath, so witnesses who create a money debt cannot.
steps.terutzMaskana: Admission creates a money debt and still brings an oath.

steps.title: Admission is special because it cannot be contradicted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls the weakness of admission: no one can contradict a person's own admission. Witnesses, however, can be contradicted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about his mouth? It cannot be contradicted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the known weakness of the admission case. This sets up the next move, which answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's own admission is completely solid, since nobody can contradict it. Witnesses can be contradicted by other witnesses, so they are weaker. That is why admission alone cannot prove the rule for witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Contradiction (by other testimony)
It is not subject to contradiction

phrases.english: What is special about his mouth?
That it is not subject to contradiction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counter-example from admission by repeating its known weakness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Admission cannot be contradicted, while witnesses can.

steps.title: One witness proves that even contradictable testimony brings an oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עד אחד can be contradicted and still obligates an oath. So being open to contradiction does not stop an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness will prove it: his testimony can be contradicted, and still he obligates an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the weakness of admission by pointing back to the single witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עד אחד is a kind of testimony that can be contradicted, and it still makes the defendant swear. So the special strength of admission is not what causes the oath. The two cases support each other: each one covers the other's weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: It is subject to contradiction
Obligates him to take an oath

steps.whatToRemember: The proof works in a chain. Each time one source is attacked for a weakness, the other source shows that weakness doesn't matter. Admission (פיו) shows a money obligation can bring an oath, and עד אחד shows testimony that can be contradicted still brings an oath.

phrases.english: One witness will prove it,
since he is subject to contradiction,
and yet he obligates him to take an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of admission by pointing to עד אחד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Admission brings an oath only because it cannot be contradicted.
steps.terutzMaskana: עד אחד can be contradicted and still brings an oath, so that is not the reason.

steps.title: One witness makes him swear on the very thing the witness spoke about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds a new difference. With עד אחד, the oath is about the same thing the witness testified about. With עדים, the oath is about the part the witnesses did not discuss, the part the borrower denied.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about one witness? There, the person swears about the very thing the witness testifies about. Can you say the same about two witnesses, where he swears about the part he denied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again on learning from עד אחד. It says the oath of עד אחד works differently from the oath we want in the עדים case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one witness says 'you owe him,' the borrower swears about that exact claim. In רבי חייא's case, the witnesses prove one part, and the oath is about a different part that nobody testified about. So עד אחד may not be a good source for an oath on an untouched part of the claim.

keyTerms.meaning: testifies
denied
swears
will you say (the same)? This is the standard way of asking whether the comparison really holds

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. With עד אחד, the oath covers what the witness said. With עדים, the witnesses already settled their part, and the oath is only about the other part, the one he denied.

phrases.english: What about one witness?
That is special, since about what he testifies
he swears.
Will you say the same about two witnesses,
where he swears about what he denied!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְעֵד אֶחָד, שֶׁכֵּן עַל מַה שֶּׁמֵּעִיד הוּא נִשְׁבָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 defended עד אחד as a source, this step attacks it from a new direction.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the עדים case from עד אחד alone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With עד אחד the oath is about the testimony itself. With עדים the oath is about the denied part, which the testimony never touched.

steps.title: Admission proves an oath can be on the denied part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from פיו, the מודה במקצת case. There, the person admits one part and swears about the part he denied. So an oath on the denied part is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: His own mouth (admission) will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difference from step 7 by pointing to מודה במקצת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מודה במקצת, the admission covers one part, but the oath is about the other part, which he denied. So the difference from step 7 does not matter. An oath can be about a part of the claim that was denied.

keyTerms.meaning: his mouth, meaning his own admission (the מוֹדֶה בְּמִקְצָת case)
will prove. It points to a known case to show a difference does not matter

phrases.english: His mouth will prove it.
phrases.notes: In מודה במקצת he admits part and swears on the part he denied, just like the עדים case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by bringing back the admission source from step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An oath may only cover what the evidence itself spoke about.
steps.terutzMaskana: מודה במקצת shows an oath can cover the denied part.

steps.title: Combining both sources with a common feature
steps.stepSummary: Since פיו and עד אחד each have their own weakness, the גמרא combines them. What they share is that both come through a claim and a denial, and the person swears. The same is true of עדים, so there too he swears.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reasoning has come back around. This case is not like that one, and that one is not like this one. What they have in common is that they come through a claim and a denial, and he swears. I too will bring the case of witnesses, which comes through a claim and a denial, and he should swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops relying on one source alone and builds a הצד השוה from both פיו and עד אחד together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source was attacked with a weakness the other does not have: admission cannot be contradicted, and עד אחד's oath is about the testimony itself. Since neither weakness appears in both, the shared feature must be the real reason for the oath: there is a claim and a denial. The עדים case also has a claim and a denial, so the oath applies there too.

keyTerms.meaning: the reasoning has come back around, so we now combine the sources
the feature of this case is not like the feature of that case
the shared feature: a proof built from the common point of two sources
a claim and a denial

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the actual derivation רבי חייא meant. It shows how a הצד השוה gets around weaknesses that knocked down each source alone.

phrases.english: And the reasoning has come back around:
the feature of this is not like the feature of that,
phrases.notes: "This" and "that" are the two sources: admission (פיו) and one witness.

phrases.english: and the feature of that is not like the feature of this.
Their common feature is

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַל יְדֵי טַעֲנָה וּכְפִירָה הֵן בָּאִין,
phrases.english: that they come through a claim and a denial,
and he swears.
I too will bring the case of witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁעַל יְדֵי טַעֲנָה וּכְפִירָה הֵם בָּאִין –
phrases.english: which come through a claim and a denial,
and so he swears.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין: לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both single sources were attacked and defended, this step combines them into one proof.
steps.raayaObject: That עדים who prove part of a claim obligate an oath on the rest.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared feature of מודה במקצת and עד אחד: both come through a claim and a denial and lead to an oath.

steps.title: With witnesses he is shown to be a denier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the הצד השוה. In both sources the person was never shown to be a liar. With עדים, the witnesses proved his denial false, so maybe he cannot be trusted to swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about their common feature? There, he was not shown to be a denier. Can you say the same about witnesses, where he was shown to be a denier?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the combined proof by pointing to something both sources share that the עדים case lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה can be broken by a feature found in both sources but missing in the new case. In מודה במקצת and עד אחד, no one proved the person a liar. With עדים, the witnesses showed his denial was false, so his oath may not be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: was established as, has the standing of
a denier, someone who falsely denies what he owes

phrases.english: What about their common feature?
That is special, since he was not shown to be a denier.
Will you say the same about witnesses,
where he was shown to be a denier?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַצַּד הַשָּׁוֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן, שֶׁכֵּן לֹא הוּחְזַק כַּפְרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the הצד השוה built in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה derivation for עדים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources involve a person who was never proven a liar. In the עדים case he was proven a denier, so his oath may not be believable.

steps.title: Someone who denies a loan is not treated as a liar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that witnesses do not make him a proven denier. רב חסדא rules that someone who denies a loan can still be a witness, unlike someone who denies a deposit. So the derivation stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with witnesses, is he really shown to be a denier? Didn't רב אידי בר אבין say in the name of רב חסדא: someone who denies a loan is still fit to be a witness, but someone who denies a deposit is unfit to be a witness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge of step 10 by quoting רב חסדא's ruling about someone who denies a loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being caught denying a loan made him a liar, he would be unfit to be a witness. רב חסדא says he stays fit for a loan, and only a deposit denier is unfit. Since our case is a loan, the borrower is not a proven denier, and the הצד השוה works.

keyTerms.meaning: a loan
a deposit, something left with a person to watch
fit to be a witness
unfit to be a witness

steps.whatToRemember: Denying a loan does not make someone a proven liar (רב חסדא), so the כפרן challenge to the הצד השוה of מודה במקצת and עד אחד fails. The גמרא tries another challenge next.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא splits loans and deposits. Only denying a loan keeps a person fit to be a witness, and our case is about a loan.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the 'proven denier' challenge and keeps רבי חייא's derivation in place for now. The next step brings one more challenge, based on הזמה, which step 13 answers.

phrases.english: But with witnesses, is he really shown to be a denier?
Didn't רב אידי בר אבין say
that רב חסדא said:
One who denies a loan
is fit to be a witness.
One who denies a deposit
is unfit to be a witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְעֵדִים מִי הוּחְזַק כַּפְרָן! וְהָאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by showing that denying a loan does not make someone a proven denier.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the claim behind the challenge, using a ruling of an אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being caught by witnesses denying a debt makes a person a proven liar who cannot swear.
steps.terutzMaskana: Denying a loan does not make someone a proven denier (רב חסדא), so the הצד השוה holds.

steps.title: A new challenge to the common feature: witnesses can be punished as false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rephrases the attack on the הצד השוה. פיו and עד אחד share something that עדים do not: they are not subject to the laws of הזמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the challenge should be put this way: the common feature of פיו and עד אחד is that neither is subject to the laws of הזמה. Can you learn from them to עדים, who are subject to הזמה?
steps.whatsHappening: The previous challenge (a proven liar cannot swear) was answered. Now the גמרא tries a different weakness in the הצד השוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הצד השוה only works if the new case shares everything important with the sources. פיו and עד אחד cannot be punished as עדים זוממין, while two עדים can. Maybe that difference matters, so you cannot learn an oath from them to עדים.

keyTerms.meaning: Refutes, challenges a derivation
The laws of witnesses proven to be false witnesses (they get the punishment they tried to cause)
Witnesses caught lying through הזמה

phrases.english: Rather, refute it like this:
What about the common feature between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means פיו and עד אחד, the two sources combined in step 9.

phrases.english: For they are not subject to the law of הזמה.
Will you say the same about witnesses
who are subject to the law of הזמה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first refutation of the הצד השוה was answered in step 11, the גמרא proposes a new refutation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The הצד השוה derivation from פיו and עד אחד to עדים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sources share a feature (not subject to הזמה) that the new case lacks, so the derivation may not carry over.

steps.title: רבי חייא does not use הזמה to break the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי חייא does not consider the laws of הזמה a valid reason to reject the derivation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. רבי חייא does not challenge a derivation based on the laws of הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brushes off the new challenge. According to רבי חייא, the הזמה difference is not the kind of difference that breaks a הצד השוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if the הזמה difference counts. רבי חייא does not accept it as a real difference: a single witness's testimony is also cancelled if other witnesses show he lied, even though he isn't punished. So the הצד השוה still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult

phrases.english: This is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא תּוֹרַת הֲזָמָה לָא פָּרֵיךְ.
phrases.english: רבי חייא does not refute based on the law of הזמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: רַבִּי חִיָּיא תּוֹרַת הֲזָמָה לָא פָּרֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הזמה challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the premise that the difference is relevant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הזמה difference between the sources and עדים breaks the הצד השוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא does not count הזמה as a refutation, so the derivation that עדים bring an oath stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The derivation of רבי חייא survives both challenges. A borrower who is contradicted by עדים on part of the loan still swears on the rest.

steps.title: Our משנה is not really like רבי חייא's case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the earlier claim (וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא) that our משנה supports רבי חייא. In רבי חייא's case only the lender has witnesses. In the משנה, both holders of the garment are equally backed, yet both swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the earlier statement that our משנה taught the same thing: are the cases really alike? In רבי חייא's case the lender has witnesses, but the borrower has no witnesses that he owes nothing. If the borrower had such witnesses, רבי חייא would not make him swear. In our משנה, just as we can see that this one is holding the garment, we can see that the other one is holding it too, and still they swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to an earlier line, וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא, which said our משנה supports רבי חייא. It argues that the משנה's case is too different to be a support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חייא's case, the oath comes because only one side has evidence. If both sides had evidence, there would be no oath. In the משנה, both sides have equal evidence, since each is visibly holding the garment, and yet they swear. So the משנה's oath works on different logic and does not prove רבי חייא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: "And our תנא also taught it": the משנה supports the ruling
Is it comparable?
Witnesses
"We are witnesses": it is plain for all to see
Lender / borrower

phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier claim, on 3a, that our משנה of two people holding a garment supports רבי חייא.

phrases.english: Here, just as we are witnesses for this one,

and even so they swear!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָאָמַר וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With רבי חייא's derivation secured, the גמרא returns to the earlier claim that the משנה supports him and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that our משנה supports רבי חייא's ruling about עדים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In רבי חייא's case the oath exists because only one side has evidence. In the משנה both sides have equal evidence and still swear, so the cases are not alike.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on רבי חייא's ruling itself. It only questions whether our משנה can be brought as support for it.

steps.title: The משנה supports a different ruling of רבי חייא: the הילך case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא was said about another ruling of רבי חייא. If someone admits fifty זוז of a hundred-זוז claim and hands it over on the spot, he must still swear about the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when "and the תנא also taught it" was said, it referred to another ruling of רבי חייא. רבי חייא said: if one says "You have a מנה of mine," and the other says "You have only fifty זוז, and here they are," he is obligated to swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves the phrase וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא to a different ruling of רבי חייא. It sets up the הילך case, which the משנה will be shown to support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the משנה does not fit the witnesses case, the גמרא links it to רבי חייא's הילך ruling. Even though the admitted part is handed over right away, the defendant still swears on the denied part. The connection to the משנה is developed in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (here, another ruling)
A sum of one hundred זוז
A silver coin (a דינר)
"Here it is": handing over the admitted amount on the spot
Obligated (here, to swear)

phrases.english: Rather, when "and the תנא also taught it" was said,
it was said about the other ruling of רבי חייא,
as רבי חייא said:
"I have a מנה in your hand,"
and the other says:
"You have only fifty זוז in my hand,
and here it is,"
he is obligated.
phrases.notes: Obligated to swear that he doesn't owe the other fifty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי אִיתְּמַר וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא אַאִידַּךְ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 14 by moving the support statement to a different ruling of רבי חייא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the statement to a different ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא was said as support for רבי חייא's ruling about witnesses on part of a loan.
steps.terutzMaskana: וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא was said about רבי חייא's הילך ruling: one who admits part and hands it over still swears on the rest.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא has two rulings here: (1) עדים on part of a loan bring an oath on the rest; (2) admitting part and handing it over (הילך) still brings an oath. Our משנה is cited as support for the second one.

steps.title: Why Handing Over the Money Still Requires an Oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי חייא's reason: saying הילך and paying on the spot still counts as admitting part of the claim, so he must swear.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Saying 'Here you are' also counts as admitting part of the claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind רבי חייא's ruling from the last step. Someone who hands over the part he admits is still treated as a מודה במקצת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that once he pays the fifty on the spot, those fifty drop out of the case and he is only denying the other fifty, which would mean no oath. רבי חייא says no: handing it over does not erase the fact that he admitted part of the claim. So the oath of מודה במקצת still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here you are.' The defendant hands over the amount he admits right away.
One who admits part of the claim. By Torah law he must swear about the rest.
Is considered like, is treated as

phrases.english: What is the reason?
'Here you are' also
is considered like one who admits part of the claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא – ״הֵילָךְ״ נָמֵי כְּמוֹדֶה מִקְצָת הַטְּעָנָה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the ruling of רבי חייא quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הילך does not remove the admitted part from the claim. The defendant is still a מודה במקצת and must swear.

steps.title: Our משנה of the Garment Supports the Ruling on הילך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the משנה of שנים אוחזין בטלית supports רבי חייא: what each person holds is like הילך, yet the משנה says he swears.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא of our משנה taught the same: 'Two are holding a garment.' Here, since each one is holding his part, it is obvious that what he holds is like 'here you are,' and still the משנה says he must swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our own משנה as support for רבי חייא's ruling about הילך. This is the real meaning of the earlier line וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the garment case, each person already has in his hands the part he is holding. That is just like a defendant who has already handed over the part he admits. Even so, the משנה requires an oath, which shows that הילך does not cancel the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We are witnesses.' It is plain and obvious to everyone.
Holds, grasps (is in possession of)
He must swear
'Two are holding a garment.' The opening case of our משנה.

steps.confusionAlert: In step 14 the גמרא said this משנה does NOT support רבי חייא's ruling about witnesses. Here it supports a different ruling of his, the one about הילך. Same משנה, different ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finally places the וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא proof where it belongs. The garment case is read as a model of הילך.

phrases.english: And the teacher of our משנה taught it too:
'Two are holding a garment.'
And here, since he is holding it,
we can see for ourselves
that what he holds is a 'here you are,'
phrases.notes: What one person is holding is already his, just as if the other one had handed it to him.

phrases.english: and yet it teaches: he must swear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for the הילך ruling explained in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא's ruling that one who says הילך must still swear.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of שנים אוחזין בטלית: what each holds is like הילך, yet each swears.

steps.title: רב ששת Disagrees: הילך Is Exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת rules that one who says הילך is exempt from an oath, because the money handed over counts as already in the lender's hands, so there is no partial admission left.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: one who says 'Here you are' is exempt. Why? Since he told him 'Here you are,' the coins he admits to are treated as if the lender already has them. About the other fifty he does not admit at all. So there is no admission of part of the claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the opposite opinion of רב ששת: הילך means no oath. It then explains his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב ששת, the admitted fifty are as good as already returned, so they drop out of the case. What is left is a claim of fifty that he totally denies. A full denial does not bring the Torah oath of מודה במקצת.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt (here, from swearing)
The lender (the one making the claim)
Holds, has in hand
Coins (זוזים)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא: הילך is still a partial admission, so he swears (supported by the garment משנה). רב ששת: הילך removes the admitted money from the claim, so he is exempt.

phrases.english: And רב ששת said:
'One who says Here you are is exempt.'
What is the reason?
Since he said to him 'Here you are,'
those coins that he admits to
are treated as if the lender already holds them.
And about those other fifty, he does not admit,
therefore there is no admission of part of the claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view to רבי חייא's ruling on הילך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who says הילך is exempt from an oath. The admitted money counts as already with the lender, and the rest is fully denied, so there is no מודה במקצת.

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב ששת can say הילך is exempt, when the משנה of שנים אוחזין בטלית requires an oath in a similar case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב ששת, our משנה is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ששת using the same משנה that was just used to support רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17 we saw that what each person holds in the garment case is like הילך, and still the משנה says he swears. That fits רבי חייא, but it seems to go directly against רב ששת, who says הילך is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty; a challenge to someone's view
Our משנה (here, שנים אוחזין בטלית)

phrases.english: But according to Rav Sheshet, the Mishnah is difficult!
phrases.notes: He means the garment case: each holder is like someone saying הילך, yet the משנה makes him swear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the proof for רבי חייא (Step 17) into a challenge against רב ששת's ruling (Step 18).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that one who says הילך is exempt from an oath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats a הילך-like situation as requiring an oath, which contradicts an exemption for הילך.

steps.title: רב ששת: the משנה's oath is a rabbinic enactment
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the oath in the משנה is a תקנת חכמים, not a Torah oath, so it says nothing about Torah-level הילך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת could say to you: the oath in our משנה is an enactment of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת defends himself by saying the oath in the משנה is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oath in the garment case was added by the חכמים, then it does not prove what the Torah says about הילך. So by Torah law רב ששת can still hold that הילך is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you; introduces a defense on someone's behalf
An enactment of the Sages; a rabbinic rule, not from the Torah

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet could say to you:
The Mishnah is an enactment of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source: the משנה's oath is rabbinic, not Torah law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's oath shows that by Torah law a הילך-like case requires an oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's oath is a תקנת חכמים, so it does not prove the Torah law of הילך.

steps.title: רבי חייא's side: rabbinic oaths are modeled on Torah oaths
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא agrees the משנה's oath is rabbinic, but argues that the חכמים would only create an oath that has a matching Torah oath, so הילך must be obligated by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does the other one (רבי חייא) respond? Yes, it is a rabbinic enactment. But if you say that by Torah law one who says הילך is obligated, it makes sense that the חכמים set up an oath similar to a Torah oath. But if you say that by Torah law הילך is exempt, would the חכמים set up an oath that has nothing like it in Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי חייא answers רב ששת, and shows that רבי חייא's proof from the משנה still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא accepts that the garment oath is rabbinic. But a rabbinic oath must be modeled on some Torah oath, and the closest match is a Torah oath in a הילך case. So the משנה still shows that by Torah law הילך requires an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? How does the other side respond?
Yes, indeed
However, but still
Similar to Torah law; the חכמים model their rules on Torah rules
That has nothing like it

steps.confusionAlert: רבי חייא does not deny that the משנה's oath is rabbinic. He agrees, and still uses it as proof, because a rabbinic oath must copy a real Torah oath.
steps.whatToRemember: Even when an oath is only rabbinic, it shows what the Torah law looks like, because the חכמים model their oaths כעין דאורייתא. That is how רבי חייא keeps his proof from the משנה.

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: The "other" is רבי חייא: how would he answer רב ששת's reply?

phrases.english: Yes, it is an enactment of the Sages.
However, granted, if you say
that by Torah law "here you are" is obligated,
the Rabbis would enact an oath similar to a Torah one;
but if you say
that by Torah law "here you are" is exempt,
would the Rabbis enact an oath
that has nothing like it in Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב ששת's escape in Step 20 and brings back רבי חייא's proof from Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that calling the משנה's oath rabbinic removes it as proof about Torah-level הילך.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Rabbinic oaths are modeled on Torah oaths, so a rabbinic oath in a הילך-like case points to a Torah oath for הילך.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that rabbinic enactments are made כעין דאורייתא lets a rabbinic law serve as evidence for what the Torah law is.

steps.title: An objection is introduced from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new challenge, this time against רבי חייא, from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a ברייתא that challenges רבי חייא's view that one who says הילך must swear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After defending רבי חייא's proof from the משנה, the גמרא now turns to attack his position. The actual content of the challenge comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי חייא's proof, the גמרא now opens a challenge against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's ruling (Steps 15-16) that one who says הילך must still swear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, quoted next, will be brought to contradict רבי חייא's ruling.
